title: Canary chaos replay and safety policy refresh
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A recent canary promotion (2026-02-26) that routed 5% production traffic to model-v2 triggered a 12-minute period of elevated 5xx errors and latency spikes for a subset of customers. The immediate mitigation was an automated rollback, but the rollback had a 90s hysteresis window that allowed a secondary burst of degraded requests during the rollback window.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency (p90) for the affected slice rose from 150ms to 1.1s.
- Error rate for model text-generation increased from 0.2% to 4.5% for impacted tenants.
- A small set of high-throughput customers saw KV cache mismatches causing repeated soft-failures and token re-generation waste.

Root cause hypothesis (multi-factor):
1) Model variant v2 changes increased per-token compute slightly and shifted sequence length distribution, which interacted poorly with our kernel selection for certain GPUs (increased queuing).
2) Shadow traffic tests had underrepresented the 512-1024 token tail and did not exercise the KV cache eviction pattern seen in production.
3) Auto-rollback hysteresis was too permissive: rollback policy allowed traffic to oscillate because of delayed metric propagation across regions.
4) Telemetry signal contract mismatch: the canary health probe used p50 latency and a coarse error-rate metric that missed early p95/p99 degradation.

Immediate actions taken:
- Automated rollback to model-v1 completed at 02:13 UTC (operator MARCO_NUDGE runbook step executed).
- Short-circuit added to routing policy for affected tenants to route to Dedicated pool in us-west-2 while root cause analysis proceeded.
- Emergency dashboard published and pager duty channel opened to coordinate mitigation.

Proposed long-term remediation (owners and due dates):
- Telemetry contract overhaul (owner: Priya Desai, due: 2026-03-18): add p95/p99, 1-minute rolling error-rate, queue-length from serving runtime, and KV-cache-keyspace contention events to canary health signal.
- Rollout hysteresis tightening (owner: Marco Nguyen, due: 2026-03-15): change rollback decision window to require 3 consecutive minutes of breach and reduce rollback ramp step from 50% of canary traffic to 20% per minute during unpromoted rollbacks.
- Shadow replay harness (owner: Sima Lopez, due: 2026-03-22): build a replay tool that consumes recorded production traces and replays them against model variants with KV cache emulation and token-length tail amplification.
- Kernel-selection guardrail (owner: Eng infra team, contact: Daniel Castro, due: 2026-03-29): fail deployment when inferred runtime kernel plan increases queuing for the 95th percentile of the tenant profile.
- Canary synthetic augmentation (owner: DX-team, contact: Rachel Kim, due: 2026-03-20): augment canary dataset with synthetic long-context prompts and KV-cache-collision cases.

Runbook updates (high-level):
- Add step to pause rollouts automatically if p99 latency increases > 2x baseline for > 60s across any region.
- Add explicit check for KV-cache mismatch events and an automated prefix flush option for tenants with excessive cache collisions.
- Document communication template for notifying impacted customers during canary failures and rollback windows.

Safety policy changes (summary):
- Canary traffic split minimum dwell time increased to 10 minutes for any promotion exceeding 2x baseline throughput.
- Introduce a staged shadow-to-canary path: shadow runs must achieve telemetry parity on p99 and error-rate before being eligible for canary.
- Auto-rollback hysteresis should be globally configurable per-release with a default conservative profile for major model architecture changes.

Test plan (MVP):
1) Run chaos-replay suite against model-v2 with 3 bucketed traffic profiles (light, typical, heavy) and 10x tail amplification for sequence length.
2) Inject synthetic KV-cache collisions in the replay harness and validate automatic prefix eviction and re-warm strategies.
3) Simulate delayed metric propagation across regions and verify hysteresis prevents oscillation using the new rollback policy.
4) End-to-end smoke: canary -> promote -> rollback cycle executed in staging with telemetry escalation to verify no staging-only signal gaps.

Artifacts and links (working list):
- Incident timeline doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/INC-2026-02-canary-replay
- Emergency dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rr_canary_incident
- Root-cause PR (kernel probe fix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821
- Shadow replay harness repo (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/shadow-replay

Acceptance criteria for closure:
- New telemetry contract merged and validated on canary run (signal parity with shadow)
- Rollback hysteresis change shipped and exercised via synthetic delayed-metric test
- Shadow replay harness able to reproduce the incident with >80% fidelity (error-mode reproduction)
- Runbook and policy doc updated and approved by SRE/Platform leads

Notes on trade-offs and open questions:
- Tightening hysteresis reduces time to rollback but increases risk of false-positive rollbacks during transient noise. We will mitigate with multi-signal voting (latency+error+queue) rather than single-signal triggers.
- Replaying production traces with KV semantics is imperfect; the team must accept a reconstruction fidelity threshold rather than perfect parity.
- Global safe defaults may slow down time-to-value for low-risk releases; expose per-project exceptions for trusted partners under an SRE-approved waiver.

Next immediate steps (owners):
- Marco Nguyen: finalize rollback hysteresis RFC and submit PR to routing policy (due 2026-03-08).
- Priya Desai: prototype telemetry collector for p99 and queue-length (POC by 2026-03-10).
- Sima Lopez: initial replay harness integration tests with recorded trace sample (by 2026-03-12).
